methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Gleb Tsipursky | Virginia’s AI training needs a first job at the other end - Augusta Free Press
signals.signal_reading: Training programs without corresponding job opportunities signal shallow adoption—people learn AI tools but lack economic infrastructure to apply capabilities, creating credentialed workers without deep implementation pathways.

signals.title: WVRIFA confirms Google is considering a data center in Roanoke County’s Wood Haven Technology Park - WSLS
signals.signal_reading: Google data center consideration in Roanoke represents infrastructure concentration that could deepen regional AI capability, but infrastructure alone without workforce development programs risks creating shallow, operations-focused rather than innovation-focused adoption.

signals.title: Virginia Tops AI Readiness as Smaller States Rise - Data Center Knowledge
signals.signal_reading: Virginia's top AI readiness ranking is driven overwhelmingly by NoVA's data center density and tech talent concentration, reinforcing the metro hub advantage while smaller regions 'rise' from much lower baselines—deepening rather than distributing capability.

signals.title: Virginia Orders AI Cybersecurity Plan as States Fill Federal Safety Gaps - PYMNTS.com
signals.signal_reading: Statewide cybersecurity plan for AI threats suggests platform-level governance approach where state government provides protective infrastructure, enabling broad but shallow AI adoption without requiring deep technical capability from individual agencies or users.

signals.title: CAREER CORNER: Greater Roanoke workforce board joins five-board Appalachian Advancement initiative - WDBJ7
signals.signal_reading: Multi-board Appalachian workforce initiative signals peer-network driven capability building across traditionally underserved regions—if connected to AI/tech skills rather than legacy industries, could distribute deep learning through collaborative regional structures.
